questions.question: The system of Binomial Nomenclature was given by:
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Binomial Nomenclature**- It is a two-term naming system that uses two different terms to name the species, plants, animals, and living organisms.
 
• The two terms consist of a **generic epithet** which is a genus (category) of that species, and a** specific epithet** that indicates the species itself.
 
• E.g. - In *Mangifera indica *(mango) the first name *Mangifera* indicated the generic name or genus while the second name indica indicates the specific epithet.
 
• **Carolus Linnaeus developed the binomial nomenclature.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• The rules of Binomial Nomenclature are:
 
• Biological names are generally in **Latin** so they are written in *italics.*
 
• They are **Latinized** or **derived from Latin** irrespective of their origin.
 
• Both the words when** handwritten** are underlined separately or printed in *italics* to indicate their Latin origin.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Charles Darwin** was a famous English biologist. He gave the concepts of** Natural selection, Adaptive radiation, **and** Darwin's theory of evolution**.
 
• **Donna Strickland**: She is a famous Canadian optical physicist. **She was awarded a noble prize in 2018 for the practical implementation of chirped pulse amplification.**
 
• **Thomas Henry Huxley**: He was an English biologist and anthropologist specializing in comparative anatomy. He is known as **"Darwin's Bulldog"** for his advocacy of Charles Darwin's theory of evolution.

4d

questions.question: The genus to which humans belong is:
questions.solution:
The correct option is __**Homo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The** genus to which humans belong** is **Homo.**
 
• Humans are **not a species**, they’re a **genus,** “**Homo”,** which is latin for “**mankind”.**
 
• All species that are** classified within the genus “Homo” are humans**, including all of the **extinct human species. **
 
• Humans, the genus** “Homo”,** belongs to the **“great apes”**, together with the **chimpanzee/pan, orangutan/pongo, and gorilla/gorilla genera.**
 
• Our specific species is **“sapiens”**, meaning something like** “wise” in latin. **
 
• There is variation among individual human beings, from size and shape to skin tone and eye colour.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms are included in Kingdom Protista as given by R Whittakar?

options.text: Unicellular algae, diatoms, slime mould and protozoans

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Unicellular algae, diatoms, slime mould and protozoans.**__

 
• Protista kingdom **single-celled eukaryotes**.
 
• Characteristics of Protista are given bellow:
 
 
• **Unicellular organism**.
 
• Normally aquatic.
 
• Reproduction: Asexual & sexual.
 
• **Well defined nucleus & membrane-bounded organelles.** 
 
 
 
• Group of Protista are given bellow:
 
 
• **Prokaryotic**: Dinoflagellate, Diatoms, Euglenoids.
 
• **Consumer**: Slime moulds, Myxomycetes.
 
• **Protozoans**: Slime moulds, Myxomycetes.
 
 

 
 

 
 
Nostoc, mycoplasma and protozoans

 
 
 
Most of the blue-green Algae that **fixes atmospheric nitrogen** belong to Nostoc group.

 
Mycoplasma, a genus of bacteria lack cell walls around their cell. It is the smallest bacterial cells can either be parasitic or saprophytic and can **survive without oxygen.**

 
Protozoans are heterotrophs and live as predators or parasites. They are believed to be primitive relatives of animals.

 
 
 

 
 
Bacteria, amoeba and protozoan

 
 
 
Bacteria have a chromosome consisting of a circular DNA molecule containing almost all the properties of genetic information necessary for their normal functions and reproduction.

 
Amoeba is eukaryotes. Amoeba can be both fungi, animals and algae.

 
 
 

 
 
Anabaena, bacteria and paramecium

 
 
 
Anabaena, blue-green genus for **nitrogen-fixing algae** with a bead or barrel-like cells with interspersed enlarged spores (heterocyst), found as plankton in shallow water and on moist soil.

 
Paramecium is a genus of unicellular ciliated protozoa, naturally found in aquatic habitats. As a shape, typically oblong or slipper with a cover of short hairy structures called cilia.

questions.question: Which of the following is the non-green heterotropic plant?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__F__**__**ungi**__.

 
• Fungi acts as principal decomposers in ecological systems.
 
 
• The scientific study of fungi is called mycology.
 
• Examples of fungi are yeasts, molds, mushrooms, symbionts of plants, animals, and other fungi, parasites, etc.
 
• They have chitin in their cell wall.
 
• Ethnomycology is the study of the historical uses and sociological impact of fungi.
 
 

Image of fungi:

 [IMAGE: https://th.bing.com/th/id/R73b98052e93b6bb3436592c3d30109f5?rik=ZNx2qzwLgfp1Ag&riu=http%3a%2f%2f2.bp.blogspot.com%2f_6sYA7Iz1xgw%2fS8vbiVAPT-I%2fAAAAAAAAOMw%2f-0p_RbI6TJU%2fs1600%2fBracket%2bFungus%2b(non-Stereum%2btype).jpg&ehk=ls0EFUQLx9YGadlKnrOLZLduFsSRWB6arOS%2f0uKlFBs%3d&risl=&pid=ImgRaw] 

 
• Ferns are members of a vascular group of the plant which reproduces via spores and have neither seeds nor flowers.
 
 
• They have specialized tissues that transport water and nutrients and have life cycles in which the sporophyte is the dominant phase.
 
• Their leaves are called megaphylls and they are more complex than the microphylls of clubmosses.
 
• Most of the ferns are leptosporangiate ferns.
 
• Some Ferns are used as food, medicine, biofertilizer, ornamental plants, and for remediating contaminated soil.
 
 

**Image of fern:**

 
• [IMAGE: https://th.bing.com/th/id/R35b956cfa65c1985669490bc7000d82e?rik=3KVetwkAvBXlSQ&riu=http%3a%2f%2fwww.askwetandforget.com%2fwp-content%2fuploads%2f2017%2f08%2ffern-frond.jpg&ehk=2U8s8Evj%2bEwd%2b2HWkHfuNfprAybAnnLH6xtzDZLAC18%3d&risl=&pid=ImgRaw] 
 
• Algae are classified as blue-green algae, red algae, brown algae, and green algae.
 
• They have the ability to do photosynthesis and they are a diverse group of aquatic organisms.
 
• Examples of algae are seaweeds, such as kelp or phytoplankton, pond scum, or the algal blooms in the lake.
 
• They are capable of producing oxygen by the method of photosynthesis.
 
• Algaes are not only helpful but also crucial for the existence of life on earth.

**Image of algae**:

 [IMAGE: https://www.lifecycleassociates.com/wp-content/uploads/2011/12/Algae_Square.jpg] 

 
• Mosses are a phylum of non-vascular plants.
 
 
• They do not grow flowers, wood, or true roots instead of seeds they reproduce by spores.
 
• They have rhizoids in place of roots.
 
• They are found in wet environments such as rainforests, wetlands, and alpine ecosystems.
 
• There are approximately 14,500 species of moss in the world which makes 75% of all bryophyte species.
 
 

**Image of mosses**:

 [IMAGE: https://sadeik.files.wordpress.com/2013/01/anomodon.jpg]

questions.question: The characteristic feature of pteridophyte is
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• Kingdom plants are divided into five groups- Thallophytes, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms, and Angiosperms.
 
• Thallophyta
 
 
• The plant body is not differentiated from roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• They are commonly called algae.
 
 
 
• Bryophyta
 
 
• These are small terrestrial plants.
 
• They show differentiation in the body design, with stem, leaf-like structures, and root-like structures.
 
 
 
• Pteridophyta
 
 
• The plant body is differentiated into roots, stems, and leaves, apart from having a specialized tissue for conduction.
 
 
 
• Gymnosperms
 
 
• Gymnosperms are plants with naked seeds.
 
 
 
• Angiosperms
 
 
• Angiosperms are seed-bearing plants. Seeds develop inside tissues that get modified to form the fruit of the plant. 
 
 

**Explanation:**__

 
• Pteridophyta: Plants from this group have well-developed roots, stem and leaves, and **separate tissues for conduction of food and water**.
 
• **They do not bear flowers and fruits.**
 
• They reproduce with the help of spores formed along the back or posterior surface of their leaves.
 
• Examples - ferns like *Nephrolepis, Marsilea, Pteris, Adiantum, Equisetum, Selaginella, Lycopodium*, etc.
 
• Thereby, all the correct answer is **''all of the above''**
